text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Rate control with metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily; no antiarrhythmic drug or cardioversion while thyrotoxic, because most thyrotoxic atrial fibrillation reverts once thyroid levels are normal; taper the beta-blocker once he is no longer thyrotoxic
  • Stroke-risk and bleeding-risk scoring (CHA2DS2-VASc 1 for age 65 to 74; HAS-BLED 1 for age over 65) with a shared decision to continue apixaban 5 mg twice daily while thyrotoxic, then reassess once sustained sinus rhythm is confirmed after he is no longer thyrotoxic
  • Methimazole 20 mg daily after a baseline blood count and liver tests, with written advice to stop it and call at once for fever, sore throat, mouth ulcers, jaundice, or dark urine; stop three days before radioactive iodine
  • Endocrinology consultation to confirm Graves' disease, assess the eyes, and choose definitive treatment (radioactive iodine, long-term methimazole, or surgery)
  • After radioactive iodine: free T4 and total T3 within one to two months and then every four to six weeks until stable; levothyroxine once hypothyroid, started below full replacement; TSH four to eight weeks after each dose change, at six months once stable, then yearly; target TSH 0.4 to 4.0 mIU/L
  • Atrial fibrillation monitoring at every visit (heart rate and rhythm, blood pressure, weight, symptoms, activity, alcohol, tobacco), ECG when indicated, echocardiogram at diagnosis, CHA2DS2-VASc and HAS-BLED yearly, creatinine and blood count at baseline and yearly on apixaban, and sleep apnea screening at diagnosis and yearly
  • Return to running in steps once the heart rate is controlled, aiming for about 210 minutes a week of moderate to vigorous activity; limit alcohol to no more than one drink a day

resource.description: Manage new paroxysmal atrial fibrillation triggered by Graves' hyperthyroidism in a fit 66-year-old: rate control with a beta-blocker and no cardioversion or antiarrhythmic while thyrotoxic, CHA2DS2-VASc and HAS-BLED scoring with a shared anticoagulation decision, methimazole pretreatment with safety monitoring, radioactive iodine as definitive treatment, recognition of the expected hypothyroidism afterwards, levothyroxine started at a cautious dose and titrated by TSH, confirmation of sustained sinus rhythm before stopping anticoagulation, on the CMID atrial fibrillation and hypothyroidism schedules with the 1988 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS and ATA guidelines.
